subject: CRITICAL: Production hit after v4.2 quant rollout
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pulseretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors after v4.2 quant rollout

Sean —

We started the v4.2 rollout with q8_2048 quant profile this morning and within ~30 minutes saw a sharp increase in 500 errors and tokenization failures for our checkout scoring endpoint. Key observations: 
- p95 baseline ~180ms, p99 jumped from ~320ms to 2.9s
- throughput for that route dropped ~40% (client-side throttling observed)
- error rate 500s climbed to ~6.8% (from <0.2%)
- some responses contain truncated text / tokenization errors (we attached a small sample and logs)

This is customer-facing on a high-volume checkout flow. Can you confirm rollback options and ETA to restore production latency? We need an immediate mitigation plan.

Attached: pulseretail-logs-0731.txt (sanitized)

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering, Pulse Retail
liam.oconnor@pulseretail.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pulseretail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors after v4.2 quant rollout

Liam — thanks for the quick signal and the logs. I’m escalating this now and we’ll treat it as a production incident. Immediate plan (we will not take any risky actions without your consent):

1) Roll traffic back to v4.1 (non-quantized variant) OR route Pulse Retail to v4.2 non-quant variant if available.
2) Create a short-lived routing policy to pin your traffic to the previous model while we triage.
3) Collect additional decoded traces and KV cache stats — Soojin will lead triage.
4) If rollback is accepted, estimate: 30–60 minutes to push the routing override and verify p99 recovery.

Please confirm: do you authorize Redwood to execute the rollback/routing override now? If you prefer we can schedule a coordinated failover with your ops team.

I’m copying Soojin and Markus to run triage and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pulseretail.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors after v4.2 quant rollout — triage notes

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Replayed a subset of the attached logs against v4.1 and v4.2(q8_2048). v4.2 shows repeated decode stalls during long-context scoring, correlated with high tail latency and token truncation.
- Error pattern: downstream 502/500s originate from our decoder worker hitting a stall waiting on quantized kernel path; memory access latencies spike for sequence lengths >1024.
- Metrics: within 20m of rollout, p99 === 2.8–3.1s, 500 errors 6–7% concentrated on hotpath. CPU/GPU utilization doesn’t show saturation — nucleus is decode path stalling.
- Hypothesis: q8_2048 path’s custom int8 kernel is hitting pathological memory access patterns for your long-tail prompts.

Mitigation options: 
A) Immediate routing override to v4.1 non-quant variant (recommended) — low risk, immediate.
B) Switch your traffic to a v4.2 variant with q4_f16 profile (if acceptable) — may require a short warm-up and runs the risk of slight quality difference.
C) Hotfix in runtime to prefer fallback decode kernel for sequences >1024 (would require a short deploy — ~3 hours including canary).

I’ve opened RINF-23456 for this incident and uploaded the sample traces. I can push the routing override now if Sean/Liam give the go-ahead. Attaching initial-triage.md with raw command outputs and sample traces.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pulseretail.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Exec summary & mitigation timeline

Team / Liam — short exec summary and ask: 

What happened: v4.2 with q8_2048 went live for Pulse Retail routing and produced decode stalls on long contexts leading to p99 latency spikes and a rise in 500s.

Impact: Customer-facing checkout flow degraded — estimated revenue impact unknown, severity HIGH.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Soojin triaged and identified kernel-level stalls.
- We proposed three mitigations (routing rollback to v4.1, switch to q4_f16, or runtime kernel fallback).
- With Sean and customer approval we will execute routing rollback now.

Timeline (if rollback approved):
- 13:30 — push routing override (canary 5% -> 100% in 20m)
- 14:00 — verify p99 and error rate; if stable, continue 1h monitoring then mark as mitigated
- 16:00 — begin post-incident capture and schedule follow-up remediation work with Platform and Research to harden q8_2048 path
Ask: Exec attention requested if this customer needs SLA credit, dedicated capacity, or product change funding. Also recommend a short-term hold on q8_2048 rollouts for other high-latency customers until we root-cause.

Attachments: postmortem-template.docx (for incident owners)
Runbook link: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops/runbooks/pulse-rollback
Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RINF-23456

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pulseretail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Resolved: rollback to v4.1 completed and validation metrics

Liam — quick update from today: 
- At 16:30 PDT we pushed a routing override for Pulse Retail to v4.1 (non-quantized) and ramped 5% -> 100% over 18 minutes.
- Observed metrics post-rollback (compared to pre-rollout baseline): p95 returned to ~170ms, p99 = 310–340ms, error rate back down to ~0.25%, throughput restored to ~98% of baseline.
- We collected decode traces and a rollback snapshot; attached rollback-snapshot.json for your ops team to review.

Next steps (short term): 
- We will keep the override in place for 48 hours while Research and Platform perform deeper kernel analysis.
- We will run a targeted test harness of q8_2048 against your long-context prompt sets in staging and share the results.
- Follow-up call: propose Thu 10:00AM PDT to review the traces and remediation plan — will send calendar invite.

We sincerely apologize for the disruption. If you prefer, we can initiate a formal SLA credit review and provide a concise incident report once postmortem is complete.

Attachments: rollback-snapshot.json
Related: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RINF-23456

Thanks for the patience — we’ll be present for the follow-up and remediation.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
